phases.message: I retire at the end of this month and I've never signed up for Part B. Start in my inbox: HR's retirement packet, the insurer's COBRA notice, Lena's note and anything else about Medicare.
Staffnest, Halberd's HR portal. Read my employment and health plan record and the documents HR posted.
Thistlewood, our insurer. Read what coverage each of us has and the plan documents.

Benefitline. Read the Part B rules and our Medicare records. Then do what has to be done now so neither of us pays a lifetime penalty or goes without coverage: get any form you need from HR, sign up whoever can sign up now, and tell me what has to wait and why. Don't sign anyone up who can't.

plan_docs.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Thistlewood plan documents for the Oduya household. Topics: group, cobra, retiree.

Halberd Logistics Employee Health Plan. For an employee over 65 still working at an employer with 20 or more employees, this plan pays first and Medicare second. Coverage ends on the last day of the month employment ends.

COBRA continuation of the Halberd plan, up to 18 months, elected within 60 days of the election notice. For a person who has Medicare, COBRA pays after Medicare; if the person could have had Part B and did not enroll, COBRA may pay only what it would have paid after Part B.

Harlow Unified School District Retiree Medical Plan. For a retiree eligible for Medicare, this plan pays after Medicare Parts A and B, as if she had both, whether or not she has enrolled in Part B. Cancelling it cannot be undone: a retiree who leaves may not rejoin.

rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Medicare Part B enrollment, under 42 CFR 406.24 and 407.20 (special enrollment period), 407.15 (general enrollment period) and 408.22 and 408.24 (late enrollment penalty). Topics: periods, sep, start, penalty, forms, not-current-employment, creditable.

Part B can be taken up in the initial enrollment period around the 65th birthday; in the special enrollment period for group health plan coverage based on current employment (sep); or in the general enrollment period, 1 January to 31 March each year, with coverage from the month after enrollment and any late enrollment penalty.

A person over 65 covered by a group health plan based on their own or their spouse's current employment, of an employer of any size, may enroll in Part B in any month they are so covered, and in the 8 months after the month that coverage or that employment ends, whichever is first (42 CFR 406.24, 407.20). After those 8 months the period is gone.

Enrolling in a month still covered by the employer plan, or in the first full month after, Part B starts on the first day of the month of enrollment or, at the person's choice, of any of the next three months (42 CFR 406.24(e)). Later in the period, it starts the month after enrollment. To leave no gap and pay no month twice, choose the month after the employer coverage ends.

The Part B premium ($202.90 a month in 2026) rises by 10% for each full 12 months a person could have had Part B and did not, for as long as they have Part B (42 CFR 408.22). Months covered by a group health plan based on current employment, and months used in a special enrollment period, are not counted (408.24).

Enroll in the special period with Form CMS-40B and proof of the group health plan coverage based on current employment: Form CMS-L564, Section B completed by the employer for each person covered by its plan, or, where the employer has not completed it, other proof of the coverage, such as pay stubs showing the plan's premium deductions, W-2s or the insurance card. Both can be submitted online. There is no fee.

COBRA continuation and retiree coverage are not coverage based on current employment. Neither opens the special enrollment period, extends it, or stops the penalty months from counting. The 8 months run from when the job or the job-based coverage ends, whether or not COBRA is taken.

Creditable coverage is a Part D term (42 CFR 423.56): drug coverage worth at least Medicare's standard drug coverage. It has nothing to do with Part B. A notice of creditable coverage is not proof of group health plan coverage for Part B.
